I had better leave him and go elsewhere.” He sheathed his sword, mounted his horse, and without waiting for dawn, made his way alone to Dong Commandery. When Cao Cao awoke and found Chen Gong gone, he reflected, “He heard those two remarks of mine, suspected me of inhumanity, and left me. I must hasten on and cannot remain here long.” He therefore traveled through the night to Chenliu, found his father, and related everything that had happened. He wished to distribute the family wealth and recruit a righteous army. His father said, “With such limited means, I fear you cannot accomplish the undertaking. There is a man here, the Filial and Incorrupt nominee Wei Hong, who is generous with his wealth and devoted to righteousness; his household is immensely rich. If you can obtain his aid, the enterprise may succeed.”

p.src: Cao Cao prepared wine and a banquet, respectfully invited Wei Hong to his home, and said, “The Han court now has no true master. Dong Zhuo has monopolized power, deceiving the sovereign and harming the people, and all beneath Heaven gnash their teeth at him. I wish to exert all my strength to uphold the dynasty, but I bitterly regret that my power is insufficient. You, sir, are a man of loyalty and righteousness; I venture to ask for your assistance.” Wei Hong said, “I have long cherished the same intention, but regretted that I had not yet encountered a hero. Since you, Mengde, possess such lofty ambition, I am willing to aid you with my family fortune.” Cao Cao was overjoyed. He first issued a forged imperial edict and dispatched messengers to every region, then began recruiting a righteous army. He raised a white recruitment banner bearing the two characters “Loyalty and Righteousness.” Within a few days, volunteers gathered as thickly as falling rain.

p.src: One day, a man from Weiguo in Yangping, surnamed Yue, named Jin, and styled Wenqian, came to join Cao Cao. Another man, from Julu in Shanyang, surnamed Li, named Dian, and styled Mancheng, also came to join Cao Cao. Cao Cao retained them both as officers of his personal staff. There was also Xiahou Dun, styled Yuanrang, a native of Qiao in Pei, who was a descendant of Xiahou Ying. From childhood he had practiced with spear and staff. At fourteen, while studying martial arts under a master, he killed a man who had insulted his teacher and fled to another region. Hearing that Cao Cao had raised troops, he and his clansman and younger cousin Xiahou Yuan each led a thousand stalwart men to join him. These two were in fact Cao Cao’s kinsmen: Cao Cao’s father, Cao Song, had originally been born into the Xiahou clan but was adopted into the Cao family, and thus they belonged to the same lineage.

p.src: Now Gongsun Zan, Administrator of Beiping, was leading fifteen thousand elite troops through Pingyuan County in Dezhou. As they marched, he saw in the distance a yellow banner amid a grove of mulberry trees, and several riders came forth to meet him. Gongsun Zan looked and saw that it was Liu Xuande. Gongsun Zan asked, “Worthy brother, why are you here?” Xuande replied, “In former days, elder brother, I was indebted to you for securing my appointment as Magistrate of Pingyuan. Hearing that your great army was passing this way, I came especially to await you and invite you into the city to rest your horses.” Pointing at Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, Gongsun Zan asked, “Who are these men?” Xuande replied, “They are Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, my sworn brothers.” Gongsun Zan said, “Are these the men who helped you defeat the Yellow Turbans?” Xuande replied, “It was entirely through the strength of these two.” Gongsun Zan asked, “What offices do they hold now?” Xuande answered, “Guan Yu serves as a mounted archer, and Zhang Fei as a foot archer.” Gongsun Zan sighed, “Truly, heroes are buried in obscurity! Now Dong Zhuo has thrown the realm into disorder, and the lords beneath Heaven are all going to punish him. Worthy brother, why not abandon this lowly office, join us in attacking the traitor, and lend your strength to upholding the Han? What say you?” Xuande replied, “I am willing to go.” Zhang Fei said, “If you had let me kill that villain then, none of today’s troubles would have arisen.” Yunchang said, “Since matters have come to this, we should make ready and depart at once.”

p.src: When he had finished reading, they smeared their lips with sacrificial blood. Moved by the impassioned spirit of his words, all wept until tears streamed down their faces. When the blood oath was concluded, they descended from the altar. They escorted Yuan Shao into the command tent and seated him, while the others took their places in two rows according to rank and age. After Cao Cao had passed the wine several rounds, he said, “Now that we have appointed a leader of the alliance, each of us must obey his commands and together uphold the realm, without disputing over who is stronger or weaker.” Yuan Shao said, “Though I lack ability, since you gentlemen have chosen me as leader of the alliance, merit shall certainly be rewarded and guilt certainly punished. The state has its established laws, and the army its discipline. Each of you must observe them and must not transgress.” All replied, “We shall obey your every command.” Yuan Shao said, “My younger brother Yuan Shu shall take overall charge of provisions and supplies, furnishing every camp and allowing none to suffer want. We also require one man to serve as vanguard and advance directly to Sishui Pass to challenge the enemy. The rest shall occupy the strategic positions and stand ready to support him.” Sun Jian, Administrator of Changsha, stepped forward and said, “I am willing to command the vanguard.” Yuan Shao said, “Wentai is brave and fierce; you are well suited to this charge.” Sun Jian therefore led the troops under his command in a swift assault toward Sishui Pass. The officers guarding the pass dispatched a courier on a fleet horse to the Chancellor’s residence in Luoyang to report the emergency. Ever since Dong Zhuo had seized supreme power, he had feasted and drunk every day. Li Ru received the urgent dispatch and went straight to report it to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo was greatly alarmed and hastily assembled his generals to deliberate. Lü Bu, Marquis of Wen, stepped boldly forward and said, “Father, do not worry. I regard the lords beyond the pass as no more than weeds. Grant me an army of tigers and wolves, and I shall cut off every one of their heads and hang them above the capital’s gate.” Dong Zhuo was overjoyed and said, “With my Fengxian beside me, I may rest easy without a care!” Before he had finished speaking, a man behind Lü Bu stepped forth and cried loudly, “‘Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken?’ There is no need to trouble the Marquis of Wen to go in person. For me to take the heads of those lords would be as easy as drawing an object from a bag.” Dong Zhuo looked at him. The man stood nine chi tall, with a tiger’s frame, a wolf’s waist, a leopard’s head, and an ape’s arms; he was a native of the lands west of the passes. His surname was Hua and his given name Xiong. Delighted by these words, Dong Zhuo promoted him to Colonel of Valiant Cavalry and assigned him fifty thousand cavalry and infantry. Together with Li Su, Hu Zhen, and Zhao Cen, he hurried through the night to the pass to meet the enemy. Among the allied lords was Bao Xin, Chancellor of Jibei. Reflecting that Sun Jian had been appointed vanguard and fearing he would seize the first merit, Bao Xin secretly dispatched his younger brother Bao Zhong with three thousand cavalry and infantry. Taking a byway, Bao Zhong went straight to the foot of the pass and challenged the enemy. Hua Xiong led five hundred armored cavalry in a flying charge down from the pass and roared, “Rebel general, do not flee!” Bao Zhong hurriedly tried to retreat, but Hua Xiong raised his blade and brought it down, cutting him from his horse; a great many officers were captured alive. Hua Xiong sent a man to deliver Bao Zhong’s head to the Chancellor’s residence and report the victory, whereupon Dong Zhuo promoted Hua Xiong to Commander-in-Chief.

p.src: Hua Xiong agreed and ordered his soldiers to eat their fill before descending from the pass by night. That night the moon shone white and the wind blew clear. It was already midnight when they reached Sun Jian’s camp; with drums and shouts, they charged straight in. Sun Jian hastily donned his armor and mounted, only to encounter Hua Xiong. Their horses crossed, but before they had fought many bouts, Li Su’s troops arrived behind and set the camp ablaze. Sun Jian’s army fled in chaos. The generals were scattered in confused fighting; only Zu Mao stayed close to Sun Jian as they broke through and fled. Hua Xiong pursued them from behind. Sun Jian took up his bow and loosed two arrows in succession, but Hua Xiong dodged them both. When he shot a third, he pulled so fiercely that his painted magpie bow snapped; he had no choice but to cast it aside and gallop away. Zu Mao said, “My lord, the red kerchief upon your head is conspicuous, and the enemy has recognized you by it. Take it off and let me wear it.” Sun Jian removed the kerchief and exchanged it for Zu Mao’s helmet; then they fled by separate routes. Hua Xiong’s troops pursued only the man in the red kerchief, allowing Sun Jian to escape by a bypath. Hard pressed by Hua Xiong, Zu Mao hung the red kerchief on the half-burned pillar of a house, then slipped into the woods and hid.

p.src: Suddenly a scout reported, “Hua Xiong has led armored cavalry down from the pass. He has Governor Sun’s red kerchief displayed on a long pole and is outside the camp hurling abuse and challenging us to battle.” Yuan Shao asked, “Who dares fight him?” Yu She, a valiant general behind Yuan Shu, stepped forward and said, “I volunteer to go.” Delighted, Yuan Shao ordered Yu She to take the field. Almost at once a report came: “Yu She fought Hua Xiong for fewer than three bouts and was cut down.” All were greatly alarmed. Governor Han Fu said, “I have a great general, Pan Feng, who can slay Hua Xiong.” Yuan Shao urgently ordered him into battle. Pan Feng took up his great axe and mounted his horse. Before long, a rider galloped back with the report: “Pan Feng too has been slain by Hua Xiong.” All present turned pale. Yuan Shao said, “What a pity my great generals Yan Liang and Wen Chou have not arrived! Had either one been here, why should we fear Hua Xiong?” Before he had finished, a man below the steps cried out, “I volunteer to cut off Hua Xiong’s head and lay it before this tent!” They looked and saw a man nine chi tall, with a beard two chi long; he had phoenix eyes and silkworm brows; his face was the hue of a dark-red jujube, and his voice rang like a mighty bell; he stood before the tent. Yuan Shao asked who he was. Gongsun Zan replied, “This is Guan Yu, brother of Liu Xuande.” Yuan Shao asked what office he presently held. Gongsun Zan said, “He serves Liu Xuande as a mounted archer.” From within the tent Yuan Shu roared, “Do you take it that none of us lords has a great general? A mere archer—how dare you speak so wildly! Throw him out!” Cao Cao hastily stopped him, saying, “Gonglu, calm your anger. Since this man has spoken so boldly, he must possess courage and strategy. Let him try his hand. If he fails, it will not be too late to punish him.” Yuan Shao said, “If we send an archer to fight, Hua Xiong will surely laugh at us.” Cao Cao replied, “This man’s bearing is uncommon. How would Hua Xiong know he is an archer?” Lord Guan said, “If I do not prevail, I ask that you take my head.”

p.src: Now the defeated troops under Hua Xiong returned and reported the disaster at the pass. Li Su hurriedly wrote an urgent dispatch and sent word to Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo hastily summoned Li Ru, Lü Bu, and the others to confer. Li Ru said, “Now that we have lost our great general Hua Xiong, the rebels’ power has grown formidable. Yuan Shao is the leader of the alliance, while his uncle Yuan Wei presently holds the office of Grand Tutor. Should they act in concert from within and without, it would place us at a grave disadvantage; we should eliminate him first. I ask that the Chancellor personally lead the main army and divide the forces to suppress them.” Dong Zhuo approved his counsel and ordered Li Jue and Guo Si to take five hundred soldiers, surround Grand Tutor Yuan Wei’s residence, and exterminate everyone there, old and young alike; Yuan Wei’s severed head was then sent ahead to the pass for public display. Dong Zhuo then raised two hundred thousand troops and advanced in two divisions: he first ordered Li Jue and Guo Si to lead fifty thousand men and hold Sishui Pass without engaging the enemy; Dong Zhuo himself took one hundred and fifty thousand men and, together with Li Ru, Lü Bu, Fan Chou, Zhang Ji, and the others, went to defend Hulao Pass. The pass lay fifty li from Luoyang. When the army reached the pass, Dong Zhuo ordered Lü Bu to take thirty thousand men and establish a great camp before it. Dong Zhuo himself remained stationed within the pass.

p.src: Swift-mounted scouts learned of this and carried the report into Yuan Shao’s main camp. Yuan Shao assembled the lords to deliberate. Cao Cao said, “Dong Zhuo has stationed his army at Hulao and cut across the center of our allied host. We should now marshal half our forces and meet him.” Yuan Shao therefore assigned eight contingents of feudal lords—Wang Kuang, Qiao Mao, Bao Xin, Yuan Yi, Kong Rong, Zhang Yang, Tao Qian, and Gongsun Zan—to meet the enemy at Hulao Pass. Cao Cao led his own army back and forth in support. Each of the eight lords set his army in motion. Wang Kuang, Governor of Henei, arrived first with his troops. Lü Bu came racing out to meet him with three thousand armored cavalry. Wang Kuang drew his troops up in battle formation. Reining in beneath the gate-banner and looking out, he saw Lü Bu ride forth: on his head was a purple-gold coronet with three-pronged ornament clasping his hair; on his body a red brocade robe of a hundred flowers from Western Sichuan; over it linked armor with beast-faced shoulder guards; and around his waist an exquisitely wrought lion-headed belt securing his armor. A bow and arrows hung at his side, and in his hand he held a painted halberd. Beneath him was the wind-neighing Red Hare. Truly, among men Lü Bu, among horses Red Hare!

p.src: Wang Kuang turned and asked, “Who dares ride out and fight?” A general behind him spurred forward, leveling his spear. Wang Kuang looked and saw that it was Fang Yue, a renowned general of Henei. Their horses met, but before five bouts had passed, Lü Bu thrust him from the saddle with one stroke of his halberd, then charged straight ahead with the weapon leveled. Wang Kuang’s army was utterly defeated and fled in all directions. Lü Bu charged and slew east and west as though no one stood in his path. Fortunately, the armies of Qiao Mao and Yuan Yi both arrived and rescued Wang Kuang; only then did Lü Bu withdraw. The forces of the three lords, each having lost some men and horses, retreated thirty li and made camp. The remaining five armies arrived afterward, and all gathered to deliberate, saying that Lü Bu was a matchless champion whom no one could withstand.

p.src: While they were still troubled over this, a junior officer reported, “Lü Bu is challenging us to battle.” The eight lords mounted together and divided their troops into eight columns, arrayed upon a high ridge. From afar they saw Lü Bu’s compact body of troops, their embroidered banners fluttering, charge the formation first. Mu Shun, a general under Zhang Yang, Governor of Shangdang, rode out with spear leveled to meet him, but Lü Bu raised his halberd and with a single stroke thrust him beneath his horse. All were greatly alarmed. Wu Anguo, a general under Kong Rong, Governor of Beihai, galloped out wielding an iron hammer. Lü Bu brandished his halberd, urged on his horse, and rode to meet him. After more than ten bouts, a sweep of Lü Bu’s halberd severed Anguo’s wrist; dropping his hammer to the ground, Anguo fled. The soldiers of all eight contingents rushed forth together and rescued Wu Anguo. Lü Bu withdrew. The lords returned to camp to deliberate. Cao Cao said, “Lü Bu’s valor is unmatched. We should assemble all eighteen lords and together devise a sound plan. If we capture Lü Bu, Dong Zhuo will be easy to destroy.”
